proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published execution satisfying the two stated support hypotheses.  By \(\textnormal{lem:lgs-case-refinement}\), the input-determined machine cannot exhaust a positive line: finite enumeration finds a supported witness whenever the displayed published predicate has one.  It therefore returns a formula, and every selected context lies in \(H\).  The same lemma, using computed fixing-order invariance and the local context and hybrid identities, gives equality of every returned district kernel with its published counterpart on the retained parameter image.  District assembly gives equality of the terminal circuits there.

Every division made by the machine is an actual context, truncated-factorization, or fixing denominator in the step-indexed ledger.  By \(\textnormal{lem:step-indexed-ledger-positivity}\),
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{7}
\]
The successful published terminal circuit equals the normalized causal target, so for \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\),
\[
 F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}=T_{a,H}^N(\eta).
\tag{8}
\]
Normalization equivalence gives
\(O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=O_H(\theta)\) and
\(T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\).  Substitution in (8) yields
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta),
 \qquad \theta\in\Theta_H.
\]
Reinserting the stored gates reverses each context substitution, while every other equality was proved after exact cross-multiplication.  Hence the machine and published circuits, and their actual positive margins, are algebraically equal modulo the original gate and response-table equations.  No unsupported context has been added.

Determinacy and nonresidual progress are \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\) and \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\).  Local soundness follows case by case.  Context evaluation and its base division are sound by \(\textnormal{lem:context-construction-soundness}\); chain-rule extraction is sound by \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\); every computed fixing quotient satisfies its cross-multiplied identity by \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\); the Algorithm-2 splice is sound by \(\textnormal{lem:hybrid-kernel-soundness}\); and final multiplication and marginalization are sound by \(\textnormal{lem:district-assembly-soundness}\).  The ledger lemma makes every division reversible on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\).  A verified residual projection satisfies
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^{N}-P(o_H^{N})=0
\]
with \(D>0\), so it emits the asserted formula.  A verified contrast satisfies the two observation identities, target inequality, simplex inequalities, exact-support signs, and cell-positivity signs before gate reinsertion; normalization equivalence transports them to the original model.  Candidate exhaustion emits only \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\), not a causal conclusion.

It remains to prove termination.  The lexicographic order on
\(\mathbb N^4\) is well founded: in an infinite descent the first coordinate eventually stabilizes, then the second, third, and fourth do likewise, a contradiction.  Associate to a task rank \((n,c,f,k)\) the ordinal
\[
 \rho(n,c,f,k)=\omega^3n+\omega^2c+\omega f+k<\omega^4.
\]
For a finite task multiset \(M\), take the natural sum
\(\Omega(M)=\mathop{\#\!\sum}_{\tau\in M}\omega^{\rho(r_I(\tau))}\).
If one task is removed or replaced by finitely many tasks of strictly smaller rank, the leading term contributed by that task disappears and all new terms have smaller exponent; hence \(\Omega\) strictly decreases.  This is exactly the Dershowitz--Manna multiset extension and proves it well founded.

Now inspect the cases.  Start and district splitting replace a task by finitely many proper-mask children, or by equal-mask administrative children with lower control level.  Advancing a phase lowers its control level.  A fixing step lowers the remaining-fix count, and its last step invokes a lower-control continuation.  A failed A2 candidate lowers the remaining-candidate count; a successful one enters lower-control hybrid fixing.  Factor and Join completion remove tasks.  Thus every nonterminal nonresidual successor strictly decreases \(\mu_H\).  A finite descent must end.  Nonresidual progress excludes every endpoint except Formula, a verified twin, or ResidualPending, and determinacy permits at most one result.

We first reduce the deterministic cases.  In the target LS-SWIG, \(A\) and \(S\) are fixed and \(W_0,Z_0\) have no children, so the observed random ancestor set of \(Y\) is \(Y^{*}=\{Y\}\), with sole district \(D^{*}=\{Y\}\).  In the unfixed selector graph, the bidirected paths induced by the shared roots \(U_0\) and \(R_0\) force the reachable closure of \(D^{*}\) to contain \(A\) and \(S\).  Thus \(C\ne D^{*}\) and \(S\in C\), so the unique case function enters Algorithm 2.  Its nonempty serious-child choice is the gate-forced \(A\) at \(\bar s=1\).  The only district that can contain \(D^{*}\) is computed from the LS-SWIG.  The path opened by the common root \(R_0\) connects \(S\) to the response of \(Y\) under the stated conditioning, so the line-7 d-separation condition fails; any remaining encoded triple either has empty serious set or fails the independently computed reachability test.  Hence the finite scan exhausts and, by input determinacy, returns exactly \(\operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^{*},C)\), followed by its residual task.

It remains to verify the residual candidate.  Let the affected baseline row success probabilities be
\[
 r=(3/4,1/4,1/4,3/4),\qquad d=(-4,-1,0,3).
\]
On all binary response tables \(f\), put
\[
 \pi_0(f)=\prod_j r_j^{f(j)}(1-r_j)^{1-f(j)},\qquad
 \delta(f)=\pi_0(f)\sum_j
 \frac{d_j\{f(j)-r_j\}}{r_j(1-r_j)},
 \qquad \pi_b(f)=\pi_0(f)+b\delta(f).
\tag{9}
\]
Independence under \(\pi_0\) gives \(\sum_f\delta(f)=0\) and
\[
 \sum_f\pi_b(f)f(j)=r_j+bd_j.
\tag{10}
\]
The smallest possible value of the sum multiplying \(b\) in (9) is
\(-16/3-4-12=-64/3\).  Thus \(0<b<1/32\) implies
\(\pi_b(f)>\pi_0(f)/3>0\) for every table.  Equations (9)--(10) give a rational-affine primitive-coordinate map inside the full canonical response simplex, not merely prescribed row marginals.

From \(S=R_0\mathbin\oplus N_S\),
\[
 P(S=0\mid R_0=0)=2/3,\quad P(S=0\mid R_0=1)=1/3,
\]
with the two probabilities reversed for \(S=1\).  In the natural context,
\(P(A=1\mid U_0=0)=1/4\) and \(P(A=1\mid U_0=1)=3/4\).  Therefore the coefficient of \(b\) in \(P(S=0,A=1,Y=1)\) is
\[
 \frac14\frac23\{\tfrac14(-4)+\tfrac34(0)\}
 +\frac14\frac13\{\tfrac14(-1)+\tfrac34(3)\}=0,
\tag{11}
\]
and, in the forced context \(A=1\), the coefficient is
\[
 \frac14\frac13(-4+0)+\frac14\frac23(-1+3)=0.
\tag{12}
\]
No \(A=0\) row is perturbed; equality of the \(Y=0\) cells follows from the unchanged \((S,A)\) margins.  Direct summation at \(b=0\) gives
\[
 (13,11,13,11,24,24)/96.
\tag{13}
\]
Equations (11)--(12) show that (13) holds throughout the box.  Its minimum is \(11/96>0\), and appending independent fair \(W_0,Z_0\) multiplies each full cell by \(1/4\).  Also \(P(S=0)=P(S=1)=1/2\), so support is exactly \(H\).

Under \(do(A=1,S=s_{\emptyset})\), \((U_0,R_0)\) remains uniform and
\[
 T_b(Y=1)=\frac12+b\frac{-4-1+0+3}{4}
 =\frac12-\frac b2.
\tag{14}
\]
The observation identities (11)--(13), the strict simplex and cell inequalities, exact selector support, and the constant-sign contrast (14) are exactly the residual verifier's tests.  Hence it accepts.  At \(b=1/64\), (14) gives \(63/128\), whereas the fixed model at \(b=0\) gives \(1/2\).

Exact support on the singleton gives
\[
 p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1.
\tag{15}
\]
Every selector multiplexer is laid back there, so it selects its natural response table.  Because \(S\) shares no latent root with \(V\), suppressing the constant selector deletes neither a substantive response coordinate nor an independence restriction among substantive roots.  Support-active normalization therefore yields exactly the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\).  Moreover,
\[
 p_\theta(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})=p_\theta(V=v),
\]
and setting \(S=s_{\emptyset}\) in the target changes no substantive equation.  Normalization equivalence then identifies \(\Phi_H\), after suppressing the constant coordinate, with the ordinary observational--interventional relation.

Now specialize the deterministic case function.  The only context is laid back, \(\operatorname{seriousSet}=\varnothing\), and the context graph is the ordinary ADMG.  Ancestor restriction and district spawning are therefore the ordinary ID cases.  The closure enumerator computes the unique ordinary reachable closure, and \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) supplies a valid order for precisely its complement.  If \(C=D^{*}\), computed fixing emits the ordinary reachable district factor.  If \(C\ne D^{*}\), separation of \(S\) from \(V\) puts the task in the \(S\notin C\) branch; success of \(\operatorname{fixSeq}_{\widetilde G}(C\setminus D^{*})\) emits the ordinary recursive factor, while failure records the same thicket/hedge pair \((D^{*},C)\) as the ordinary recursion.  Truncated factorization never enters as selector hybridization because there is no serious selector child.

Thus, by induction on the ordinary recursion tree, every case, computed graph, fixed set, kernel quotient, and terminal success or hedge is identical to the Shpitser--Pearl ID case.  The cited ordinary ID classification identifies those endpoints as formula or hedge.  This is a structural specialization of \(\operatorname{next}_I\); it neither assumes inclusion in a residual candidate list nor uses the unresolved fixed-support residual dichotomy.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite canonically encoded input \(I\), all ancestor, descendant, nondescendant, district, strict-parent, d-separation, laid-back, serious-set, support, and compatibility predicates used by \(\operatorname{next}_I\) are decidable.  Every enumerated candidate family is finite, and every nonempty such family has a unique canonically least member.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: By \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\), the vertex set and each value set in \(G^{+}\) are finite.  A directed ancestor or descendant predicate is decided by enumerating directed paths of length at most the number of vertices; a district predicate is decided by enumerating bidirected paths of the same bounded length.  Strict parents are read from the finite edge table.  For d-separation, enumerate the finitely many simple paths and check the collider/noncollider condition after computing the finite ancestor set of the conditioning set.  The definitions of laid-backness, compatibility, and \(\operatorname{seriousSet}\) are finite Boolean tests on selector coordinates.  The graph \(G[s]\) is obtained by a finite pass over the labelled edge list followed by finite deduplication.  Subsets, permutations, districts, contexts in \(H\), and supported triples therefore form finite encoded lists.  The bit-string encoding \(\operatorname{enc}_H\) induces a total lexicographic order, so a nonempty finite list has exactly one least member.  Every assertion follows from these explicit finite procedures.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(D\subseteq\operatorname{random}(G)\), the family of reachable supersets of \(D\) is nonempty and closed under finite intersections.  Consequently \(\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\) is the unique inclusion-minimal reachable superset used by the recursive fixing construction, and \(\operatorname{fixSeq}_G\{\operatorname{random}(G)\setminus\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\}\) returns a valid sequence.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The whole set \(\operatorname{random}(G)\) contains \(D\) and is reachable by the empty sequence, so the enumerated family is nonempty.  We first prove the persistence fact needed for intersections.  Fixing a vertex removes arrowheads into that vertex and never adds an edge or a directed path.  Hence, for any still-random \(W\), both its district and its descendant set can only shrink.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{dis}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}(W)=\{W\}
\]
continues to hold after any other valid fixing step.  If \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are reachable, take valid sequences with supports \(F_i=\operatorname{random}(G)\setminus R_i\).  Execute the first sequence and then append, in the order of the second sequence, the members of \(F_2\setminus F_1\).  Each appended vertex was fixable after its earlier predecessors in the second sequence, and the extra fixings from the first sequence only shrink its district and descendant set; hence the appended sequence is valid.  Its support is \(F_1\cup F_2\), so its remaining random set is \(R_1\cap R_2\).  Induction gives closure under every finite intersection.

There are finitely many reachable supersets of \(D\).  Their intersection \(C_0\) is reachable by the preceding paragraph, contains \(D\), and is contained in every reachable superset.  It is therefore the unique inclusion-minimal reachable superset.  The enumerator defining \(\operatorname{closure}_G(D)\) must select \(C_0\); the encoding tie-breaker is never semantically needed.  By the definition of reachability, the displayed call to \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) is not \(\operatorname{none}\), and by construction the returned sequence passes \(\operatorname{valid}\).

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite canonically encoded input \(I=(G^{+},H,A,a,Y,p_H)\), there is a unique initial state \(\operatorname{init}_H(I)\) and a total deterministic case function \(\operatorname{next}_I\).  If two inputs and current states are equal field by field, their successors and emitted results are equal.  For every \(m\ge0\), the run prefix of length \(m\), whenever not already terminal, is a function only of \(I\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The definition of \(\operatorname{init}_H\) assigns a displayed value to each state field, so existence and uniqueness are immediate.  Consider a current state.  Its result belongs to the finite tagged sum in \(\textnormal{def:input-task-state}\).  A Formula or ResidualPending result is terminal; each LGS failure tag has the unique clause that creates its residual task and restores the running control.  Otherwise the finite work multiset is canonically encoded.  Its least enabled task is unique by \(\textnormal{lem:finite-graph-primitives}\); the encoding places every producer before a Join waiting for that producer.  The task tag selects one disjoint clause of \(\operatorname{next}_I\).

Within that clause, all graph predicates and all lists of districts, contexts, triples, permutations, and residual candidates are finite and decidable by \(\textnormal{lem:finite-graph-primitives}\).  The closure and its fixing sequence are uniquely computed by \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\).  Every successful search returns its unique canonical minimum, and every failed search selects the uniquely prescribed failure tag.  Kernel marginalization, conditioning, multiplication, substitution, and cross-multiplication are arithmetic operations on finite tables or finite rational circuits, hence are total once the clause's recorded positive denominator test passes.  Failure of that test has the uniquely specified internal-rejection result and is not a semantic alternative.  Thus exactly one clause supplies exactly one successor or result.  No clause reads a published formula, a successful derivation, extensional target equality, or an oracle agenda.

Fieldwise equal inputs and states have equal encoded lists, Boolean test values, canonical minima, arithmetic circuits, ledger entries, and continuations, so they have equal successors and results.  Finally, the prefix assertion follows by induction on \(m\).  At \(m=0\) it is the unique initial state.  If the prefix through \(m\) is a function of \(I\), applying the deterministic \(\operatorname{next}_I\) to its last nonterminal state makes the prefix through \(m+1\) a function of \(I\).

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(s\in H\), the mechanically constructed graph \(G[s]\) and initialized kernel \(q_s(v)=p_H(v,s)/p_H(S=s)\) equal the graph and conditional law obtained by evaluating the known selector gates at \(s\).  The ledger base denominator is strictly positive, and no value of \(S\) outside \(H\) is introduced.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
At a selector-controlled vertex \(X\), \(\textnormal{ass:known-selector-gates}\) makes its equation the known zero--one multiplexer.  If the intervention-status coordinate at \(s\) is one, evaluation replaces the natural row by the point mass at its recorded forced value and deletes every labelled edge disabled by that serious variable.  If the coordinate is zero, the natural row and every edge whose remaining label is satisfied persist.  Erasing satisfied labels and deduplicating does not change adjacency.  Applying this argument once to each finite gate proves that the recursively evaluated structural graph is exactly \(G[s]\), and substitution into children proves equality of the induced table.

For \(s\in H\), exact selector support gives \(p_H(S=s)>0\).  More explicitly,
\[
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})}p_H(v,s),
\]
and the sum is nonempty and strictly positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Division therefore gives the genuine conditional kernel.  Its ledger entry has precisely this cell set and identity.  Since the context enumerator ranges over \(H\), no unsupported selector value can occur.

added_lemmas.statement: For every positive finite kernel \(q\), \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}(q,B)\) equals the corresponding ordered conditional factor of \(q\).  Each conditioning denominator is its actual marginal, is a nonempty sum of positive current-kernel cells, and is recorded without changing the graph or fixed set.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(B=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) in the restriction of \(\prec\).  Finite marginalization gives the prefix marginals \(q_i(x_1,\ldots,x_i)\), with \(q_0=1\).  Positivity of current-kernel cells makes every required \(q_{i-1}\) a nonempty positive sum.  Therefore
\[
 q(X_i=x_i\mid X_1=x_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}=x_{i-1})
 =\frac{q_i(x_1,\ldots,x_i)}{q_{i-1}(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})}.
\]
Multiplying from \(i=1\) to \(m\) cancels adjacent prefix marginals and yields \(q_m\), the required ordered factor.  This proof uses only sums and conditional ratios of \(q\); it neither tests fixability nor alters an edge or a fixed vertex.  Recording each \(q_{i-1}\) with its defining marginal identity supplies exactly the asserted ledger data.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(q\) is a current kernel induced by a parameter in the compatible normalized model and \(\pi=\operatorname{fixSeq}_G(T)\ne\operatorname{none}\), stepwise execution of \(\operatorname{Fix}(G,q,\pi)\) is well defined on the ledger-positive domain, uses the actual current nested conditional at each step, and preserves the represented kernel relation after each displayed cross-multiplication.  For such a kernel, any two valid sequences with support \(T\) yield the same final kernel and CADMG.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\pi=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)\).  Validity gives
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i)=\{W_i\}
\tag{1}
\]
in the CADMG \(G_{i-1}\) present at step \(i\).  The current finite kernel \(q_{i-1}\) determines, by marginalization, the actual conditional
\[
 c_i=q_{i-1}\{W_i\mid
 \operatorname{nd}_{G_{i-1}}(W_i),
 \operatorname{fixed}(G_{i-1})\}.
\]
Its denominator and every marginal used to form it are recorded in the ledger.  On the ledger-positive domain set \(q_i=q_{i-1}/c_i\).  Then
\[
 c_iq_i=q_{i-1},
\tag{2}
\]
so the successor circuit represents exactly the fixed kernel after cross-multiplication.  In the recursive response expansion, independent latent-root factors can be grouped by districts.  Condition (1) says that no other member of the current district is a descendant of \(W_i\); summing the grouped finite factorization in topological order isolates precisely \(c_i\).  Removing that factor and all arrowheads into \(W_i\) therefore gives the CADMG kernel represented by \(q_i\).  This derives the fixing identity from the recursive equations and root factorization rather than identifying \(c_i\) with a generic margin.

For order invariance, two simultaneously valid next vertices have conditional factors drawn from the same topological quotient.  If they are in distinct districts, the grouped factors are disjoint and the two divisions commute.  If they are in one district, simultaneous fixability and (1) exclude a directed path from either to the other inside that district; finite marginalization of the common quotient then gives
\(c_Wc_{Z\mid W}=c_Zc_{W\mid Z}\), so the two cross-multiplied two-step kernels agree.  By repeatedly exchanging adjacent out-of-order vertices, any two valid permutations of the same finite support are connected without changing the quotient.  Both remove the same incoming arrowheads, so their final CADMGs and kernels agree.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever an Algorithm-2 triple passes its displayed d-separation test and its independently computed reachability test, the hybrid product \(q_{D'}^{\bar s,z}\) constructed by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\), followed by fixing along the computed \(\pi'\), equals the required district kernel \(q_{D^{*}}\) on every compatible normalized model.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a passing triple.  Districts partition the vertices of the finite LS-SWIG, so at most one district contains \(D^{*}\); acceptance establishes existence, hence the computed \(D'\) is unique.  The recursive equations and independent latent roots give the finite global Markov factorization of the LS-SWIG: this follows directly by multiplying the root probabilities and deterministic response indicators and summing latent roots not appearing in the queried margin.  The verified d-separation therefore implies
\[
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{de}(S)\}
 \mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}S
 \mid
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{nd}(S)\}
 \cup\operatorname{spa}(D').
\tag{3}
\]
Consequently the descendant factors may be evaluated at \(S=\bar s\), while the nondescendant factors retain their unconditioned chain factors, without changing the joint kernel conditional on the variables on the right of (3).  Compatibility permits the common substitution \(Z=z\) and the required coordinates of \(a\).

By \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\), the two canonically ordered products in the definition of \(q_{D'}^{\bar s,z}\) are exactly those chain factors; no fixing premise was used in forming them.  Independently, acceptance computed
\(\pi'=\operatorname{fixSeq}_{(\widetilde G[\bar s](\bar s))_{D'}}(D'\setminus D^{*})\).
The sequence is valid by its construction, so \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\) applies stepwise and removes exactly \(D'\setminus D^{*}\).  The resulting graph has random set \(D^{*}\), and the resulting quotient is the displayed \(q_{D^{*}}\).  Equations (2)--(3) show equality for every parameter satisfying the retained constraints.

added_lemmas.statement:
If every district task for \(G^{+}_{Y^{*}}\) returns a sound factor \(q_{D^{*}}\), the Join circuit
\(\sum_{Y^{*}\setminus Y}\prod_{D^{*}}q_{D^{*}}\), with the recorded treatment and context substitutions, equals the normalized target distribution.  If a district returns a failure tag, assembly emits no formula and propagates the least tag.

At \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), every entry of the step-indexed ledger is strictly positive.  Hence every division made by context initialization, \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\), or computed fixing is legal, and every returned formula satisfies \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  No common numerical lower bound is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We induct on the ledger index.  For a base entry at \(s\in H\),
\[
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})}p_H(v,s)>0
\tag{5}
\]
by exact selector support and admissible-cell positivity.  Suppose all earlier entries are positive.  A conditioning marginal introduced by \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\) is, by construction, a nonempty sum of cells of the current positive kernel.  A fixing conditional is constructed from current-kernel marginals, and its recorded numerator is likewise a nonempty sum.  After substituting the current kernel's rational expression in \(p_H\), the verifier records the exact factorization
\[
 d_j=c_j\prod_{i<j}d_i^{m_{ij}}prod_{r=1}^{R_j}
       \left(\sum_{c\in C_{jr}}K_{jr}(c)\right),
\qquad c_j\in\mathbb Q_{>0},\quad C_{jr}\ne\varnothing,
\tag{6}
\]
after cancellation and sign normalization.  Every earlier factor is positive by induction, and every last sum is positive because its cells are branch-reachable positive kernel cells.  Thus \(d_j>0\).  This proves the induction.

The terminal denominator registry is a sublist of the ledger, so all its entries are positive at \(O_H(\theta)\).  Required observed cells are positive by the model class.  The definition of \(\mathfrak D_H\) now gives \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Because the argument uses only strict inequalities at the fixed law, it supplies no uniform lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement: From every reachable state with result \(\operatorname{Running}\) and a nonresidual work task, \(\operatorname{next}_I\) has a unique successor.  That successor either completes a task, replaces it by finitely many strictly lower-ranked tasks, shortens a computed fixing sequence or candidate list, or creates an explicitly tagged residual task.  No graphical or kernel choice is supplied by an oracle.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Take the canonically least task.  A Start task computes \(Y^{*}\) and its finite district partition, so it creates the displayed children.  A District test computes the finite set \(L(D^{*})\): emptiness produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailPos}\), while nonemptiness stores its unique ordered list.  By \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\), the closure always exists and its complement has a returned valid fixing sequence.  If \(C=D^{*}\), that sequence is executed and yields a factor.  If \(C\ne D^{*}\) and \(S\notin C\), the finite context scan either finds its first valid sequence or exhausts and produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailThicket}\).

If \(S\in C\), \(\operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)\) is computable.  Its emptiness produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailHedge}\).  Otherwise the supported triples form a finite encoded list.  For its head triple, the district containing \(D^{*}\), if any, is unique because districts partition vertices.  D-separation and the independent \(\operatorname{fixSeq}\) call are decidable.  Failure removes that head candidate; success constructs the hybrid factor and then executes the returned sequence.  Exhaustion produces \(\operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}\).  A Fix task either removes the head of an already computed sequence or invokes its continuation.  A Factor stores its value.  A Join whose producers are complete either assembles or propagates the least failure; the encoding never selects a blocked Join before an extant producer.  These disjoint cases exhaust every nonresidual task.  All choices are the canonical finite computations proved deterministic in \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).

added_lemmas.statement: Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser recursively construct systematic-selection identifying kernels by ancestor restriction, district decomposition, reachable closure and fixing, supported laid-back contexts, and the displayed Algorithm-2 conditional-independence and reachability search; their successful return is an identifying functional for the causal query.

attestation.note: Primary-source handle supplied; the claim is scoped to the algorithms' displayed successful cases and soundness result.

added_lemmas.statement: For every successful support-licensed execution of Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser Algorithms 1--2, the input-determined case function reaches a formula result.  At every existential line its canonical enumeration selects a witness whenever one exists; its returned factor kernels agree with the published kernels on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\), independently of valid fixing order, and it never selects a context outside \(H\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Proceed simultaneously over the finite published recursion tree and the machine work multiset.  Both start from the same LS-SWIG, ancestor set \(Y^{*}\), and canonically computed district partition.  Suppose corresponding district tasks have been reached.  The predicates defining \(L(D^{*})\), the reachable closure \(C\), the cases \(C=D^{*}\) and \(S\in C\), and \(\operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)\) are identical displayed predicates.  The closure lemma proves that the machine's finite enumeration returns the same unique closure and a valid sequence.  If the published successful branch has a supported context or Algorithm-2 triple satisfying its line predicate, that object occurs in the machine's finite list; therefore the canonical scan finds a passing object no later than exhaustion.  The machine cannot enter the associated failure branch.

The chosen witness need not be the first witness displayed in a paper derivation.  For a different valid fixing order with the same fixed set, \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\) proves equality of the final kernel.  For two passing contexts or Algorithm-2 triples, \(\textnormal{lem:context-construction-soundness}\) and \(\textnormal{lem:hybrid-kernel-soundness}\) prove that both observable expressions equal the same normalized district kernel; after cross-multiplication their difference is zero modulo the retained constraints.  Thus the machine's canonical choice and the published choice agree on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\).  The truncated factors agree by \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\), and the joins agree by \(\textnormal{lem:district-assembly-soundness}\).

Induction over completed tasks now shows that every machine factor equals its published counterpart on the compatible image and that every ledger divisor is the actual divisor of that factor.  The successful recursion is finite, and \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) rules out diversion to a nonresidual stuck state.  Therefore the machine reaches a formula.  Every enumerated context lies in \(H\) by construction.

\]

\[

\]

\[

\]

\]
If it is empty, record \(\operatorname{LGSFailHedge}(D^{*},C)\) and create its residual task.  Otherwise enumerate all supported compatible triples \((\bar s,Z,z)\), where \(\bar s\in H\) is laid back for \(D^{*}\),

proposed.construction:
For a CADMG \(G\) and a sequence \(\pi=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)\), let \(\operatorname{valid}_G(\pi)\) recursively check, in the graph obtained after fixing \(W_1,\ldots,W_{i-1}\), that
\[

\]
For \(T\subseteq\operatorname{random}(G)\), \(\operatorname{fixSeq}_G(T)\) enumerates all permutations having support exactly \(T\), retains the valid ones, and returns the least one under the input encoding, or \(\operatorname{none}\).  Put
\[
 \operatorname{reachable}_G(R)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{fixSeq}_G\{\operatorname{random}(G)\setminus R\}
 \ne\operatorname{none}.
\]

proposed.name: computed closure and valid-sequence fixing transition
proposed.construction:
The relation \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\) implements computed closure and fixing.  For a district \(D^{*}\), compute \(C=\operatorname{closure}_{G^{+}}(D^{*})\) and the returned sequence
\(\pi_C=\operatorname{fixSeq}_{G^{+}}(V\setminus C)\).  If \(C=D^{*}\), execute the returned sequence stepwise on \((G^{+},p_H)\), choose the least \(s\in L(D^{*})\), evaluate the kernel at \(S=s\) and at the required coordinates of \(a\), and create \(\operatorname{Factor}(D^{*},q_{D^{*}},s)\).  If \(C\ne D^{*}\), execute \(\pi_C\) to obtain exactly
\[
 \widetilde G=\phi_{V\setminus C}(G^{+}),\qquad
 \widetilde q=\phi_{V\setminus C}(p_H;G^{+}).
\]
If \(S\notin C\), enumerate \(s\in L(D^{*})\), compute \(\widetilde G[s]\), and test \(\operatorname{fixSeq}_{\widetilde G[s]}(C\setminus D^{*})\).  The first successful context is executed and emits
\[
 q_{D^{*}}=\phi_{C\setminus D^{*}}(\widetilde q;\widetilde G[s]).
\]
If none succeeds, record \(\operatorname{LGSFailThicket}(D^{*},C)\) and create its residual task.  If \(S\in C\), create the Algorithm-2 task.  A \(\operatorname{Fix}(G,q,T,\mathrm{continuation})\) task always uses the already computed least valid sequence, processes one member, records its actual conditional and cross-multiplied successor identity, and then either recurs on the shorter sequence or invokes its continuation.

proposed.name: Algorithm-2, factor, and Join transition
proposed.construction:
The relation \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\) implements Algorithm 2, factor storage, ancestor marginalization, and final assembly.  For \((D^{*},C,\widetilde G,\widetilde q)\), first compute
\[
 \operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)=\operatorname{ch}_{\widetilde G}(S)\cap(C\setminus D^{*}).
\]
If it is empty, record \(\operatorname{LGSFailHedge}(D^{*},C)\) and create its residual task.  Otherwise enumerate all supported compatible triples \((\bar s,Z,z)\), where \(\bar s\in H\) is laid back for \(D^{*}\),
\(Z=\operatorname{seriousSet}\{\bar s,\operatorname{ch}^{*}(S)\}\ne\varnothing\), and \(z\) is its forced value.  Construct \(\widetilde G^{+}(\bar s)\), compute its districts, and retain a triple only if its unique district \(D'\) containing \(D^{*}\) exists and both
\[
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{de}(S)\}
 \mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp} S
 \mid
 \{D(\bar s):D\in D'\cap\operatorname{nd}(S)\}
 \cup\operatorname{spa}(D')
\]
holds by d-separation and
\(\pi'=\operatorname{fixSeq}_{(\widetilde G[\bar s](\bar s))_{D'}}(D'\setminus D^{*})\ne\operatorname{none}\).
For the first passing triple, use \(\operatorname{TF}_{\prec}\), not fixing, to form
\[
 q_{D'}^{\bar s,z}=
 \prod_{D\in D'\cap\operatorname{de}(S)}
 \widetilde q\{D\mid S=\bar s,\operatorname{pre}_{\prec}(D)\}\big|_{Z=z}
 \prod_{D\in D'\cap\operatorname{nd}(S)}
 \widetilde q\{D\mid\operatorname{pre}_{\prec}(D)\}\big|_{Z=z},
\]
and then execute \(\pi'\) to emit
\[
 q_{D^{*}}=
 \phi_{D'\setminus D^{*}}
 \{q_{D'}^{\bar s,z};(\widetilde G[\bar s](\bar s))_{D'}\}.
\]
Exhaustion records \(\operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^{*},C)\) and creates its residual task.  A factor task stores its labelled factor.  Once all factors are present, \(\operatorname{Join}\) emits
\[
 \sum_{Y^{*}\setminus Y}\prod_{D^{*}}q_{D^{*}},
\]
with each factor evaluated at its recorded context and at \(a\) on \(A\cap\operatorname{spa}_{G^{+}}(D^{*})\).  A least failure tag is propagated instead of joining whenever a district failed.

proposed.name: tagged residual certificate-verification transition
proposed.construction:
The relation \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\) receives only \(\operatorname{Residual}(\mathrm{tag},\mathrm{payload})\) tasks produced by an explicit LGS failure or irreducible residual.  It constructs the finite encoded projection and signed canonical-row-swap candidate lists from that payload and tests them in canonical order.  A projection \(P/D\) passes only if every divisor occurs in the ledger and
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^{N}-P(o_H^{N})=0
\]
after exact cross-multiplication modulo the retained constraints.  A pair of rational affine primitive-coordinate maps on a rational open box passes only if substitution gives identical observation polynomials, a nonzero target polynomial of constant certified sign, simplex membership, strictly positive admissible cells, and selector mass positive exactly on \(H\).  A passing projection emits \(\operatorname{Formula}(F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\); a passing contrast is reinserted by \(\rho_H\) and emits the global-twin certificate.  If no candidate passes, the result is \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}(\mathrm{tag},\mathrm{payload})\).  An LGS failure tag alone is never interpreted as a nonidentification certificate.

proposed.name: deterministic Algorithms 1--2 task machine
proposed.construction:
Define \(\operatorname{next}_I\) by exhaustive case analysis on the canonically least current work task and the result.  It implements Algorithm 1 lines 1--18 and Algorithm 2 lines 1--9 exactly as specified in the four transition definitions.  It computes every closure, district, context graph, d-separation test, valid fixing sequence, truncated factor, hybrid kernel, and continuation from \(I\) and the current state fields.  A failed LGS line creates the correspondingly tagged residual task; an invariant failure after a computed valid sequence is an internal rejection of the purported state, not a semantic branch.  Candidate exhaustion yields \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\).

For a task \(\tau\), let
\[
 r_I(\tau)=
 (|\operatorname{random\ ambient}(\tau)|,
   c(\tau),f(\tau),k(\tau))
\]
with lexicographic order, where the finite control levels strictly descend through
\[
 \operatorname{Start}>\operatorname{District\ tests}>
 \operatorname{closure\ fixing}>\operatorname{postclosure}>
 \operatorname{A2\ scan}>\operatorname{hybrid\ fixing}>
 \operatorname{Factor}>\operatorname{Join},
\]
\(f\) is the remaining fixing-sequence length, and \(k\) is the remaining candidate count.  The machine measure \(\mu_H\) is the Dershowitz--Manna finite-multiset extension of this rank over \(\operatorname{Work}\).  The canonical encoding orders productive tasks before a dependent Join and orders every set, sequence, and candidate topologically and then lexicographically.  The machine starts at \(\operatorname{init}_H(I)\) and iterates \(\operatorname{next}_I\) until a formula, a verified twin, or a residual-pending result is returned.

proposed.name: ledger-projected positive execution domain

After cancellation and sign normalization, each \(d_j\) retains its exact cross-multiplied identity, earlier-entry dependencies, nonempty reachable-cell set, and verified factorization into a positive rational constant, earlier positive entries, and positive kernel-cell sums.  Define
\[
 \mathfrak D_H=
 \{q\in\Delta(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}):q(c)>0
 \text{ for every branch-required cell and }d_j(q)>0
 \text{ for }j=1,\ldots,R\}.
\]
The emitted rational circuit \(F_H\) is evaluated only on \(\mathfrak D_H\).

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model and Algorithms 1--2. The present positive result is a line-by-line, input-determined refinement: every graph, context, closure, fixing sequence, hybrid factor, and denominator is computed from the finite input and current state, and every successful support-licensed branch is preserved. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the ordinary ID formula-or-hedge endpoint; the new machine specializes structurally to that recursion when the selector is constant and separated.
